amendments.because: The cache is the provable fix for the npm timeouts; the longer test timeout and the vanished-file skip are small test-support changes with no rule of their own
amendments.done_when: The Node client tests keep npm's download cache between CI runs and give a cold download enough time, and the leftover-process scan skips files that disappear while it runs

done_when: Forge's own pull request checks keep npm's download cache between runs

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. The cache added at `.github/workflows/forge.yml:42` runs only for pull requests. GitHub [scopes a pull request cache to that PR's merge ref](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching#restrictions-for-accessing-a-cache), so another PR cannot restore it. Forge's main-branch workflow downloads Jest and Vitest at `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:100-102` but does not save an npm cache. Every new Forge PR therefore starts with cold downloads in its test groups, leaving the reported timeout scenario in place. The named proof at `tests/test_fix_gate_on_split_checks.py:94` checks for the cache path but cannot catch this scope gap.
findings.title: Not done: Forge's own pull request checks keep npm's download cache between runs

why: Pull request test groups time out while npm downloads jest or vitest, and a leftover-process scan fails when a git folder vanishes mid-scan
